guide.title: Korean BBQ in Manhattan: West 32nd Street, Fifth Avenue and Five Rooms Beyond Koreatown
guide.intro: Eighteen Manhattan restaurants cook Korean barbecue on a grill at the table, and thirteen of them stand inside six blocks. Six sit on West 32nd Street between Fifth Avenue and Broadway, from Jongro BBQ on the second floor at number 22 to Gaonnuri on the 39th floor at 1250 Broadway, whose entrance is on that street. Seven more stand a block east and south, on Fifth Avenue between 31st and 32nd Streets and on East 31st and East 32nd Streets themselves. Five stand outside Koreatown: Yoon Haeundae Galbi on West 36th Street, Don Don on West 43rd, Golden HOF on West 48th, Nubiani's second room on East 58th, and COTE Korean Steakhouse on West 22nd Street in the Flatiron District. New Wonjo burns charcoal rather than gas; COTE sets a cooktop into every table.

sections.heading: West 32nd Street: Fifth Avenue to Broadway
sections.body:
Six of the eighteen stand on West 32nd Street between Fifth Avenue and Broadway.

Jongro BBQ takes the second floor at 22 West 32nd Street, where marinated ribeye, skirt steak, short rib and chuck are grilled tabletop and served with banchan, and the staff work the tongs. Jongro BBQ Market is a separate room with its own door on the first floor at 39 West 32nd Street, where guests do the grilling at the table on an all-you-can-eat price; service runs to midnight Sunday through Thursday and to 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday. New Wonjo is at 23 West 32nd Street, and it burns charcoal rather than gas under the grill at the table.

miss KOREA BBQ runs three floors at 10 West 32nd Street, with a hood over the grill at every table and the first floor given to barbecue seating. Antoya is at 37 West 32nd Street, where the cuts come out raw and the meat is grilled at the table; service runs to 11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and to 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday. Gaonnuri is on the 39th floor at 1250 Broadway, with its entrance on West 32nd Street, and tabletop grilling is the focus of the room.

sections.heading: Fifth Avenue and East 31st and 32nd Streets
sections.body:
Seven stand a block east and south of West 32nd Street, four of them on one stretch of Fifth Avenue.

Let's Meat is at 307 Fifth Avenue, where the operator states it serves table Korean barbecue exclusively, on a Cap-Style grill imported from Korea that drains the fat off as the meat cooks at the table. Gopchang Story takes the second floor at 312 Fifth Avenue, where staff crisp the beef intestine on the grill at the table. Nubiani takes the third floor at 315 Fifth Avenue, where the operator's own line reads "The grill is only one part of the table" and staff cook the sliced meat over the fire. LOVE Korean BBQ is at 319 Fifth Avenue, where the meat and a spread of vegetables go on the grill at the table, and an all-you-can-eat option runs at $100 per person.

Three more sit on the cross streets. Ahgassi Gopchang is at 1 East 32nd Street, where a slotted circular grate is recessed flush into the tabletop with raw sliced beef laid across it and banchan set around its rim. Howoo is at 7 East 31st Street, where a grill is set into the center of the table and several rounds of food arrive before the beef reaches it. Dons Bogam BBQ & Wine is at 17 East 32nd Street, where tabletop grills sit beside floor-level seating and an open kitchen, with a two-order minimum on the barbecue.

sections.heading: Beyond Koreatown: West 22nd Street to East 58th
sections.body:
Five stand outside the Koreatown blocks, spread from West 22nd Street to East 58th.

Yoon Haeundae Galbi is at 8 West 36th Street, between Fifth and Sixth Avenues in the Garment District, where a round grill is set flush into the center of each banquette tabletop and the extraction ducting runs down under the table base. Don Don is at 37 West 43rd Street, from chef Sungchul Shim, where guests grill the pork cuts at the table in a narrow room. Golden HOF / NY Kimchi is at 16 West 48th Street: downstairs, some tables carry a grill in the table itself, while the upstairs room is a pub-like bar without them.

Nubiani's second room is at 243 East 58th Street, covered by the same operator line as the Fifth Avenue floor, so the grill sits in the table there too. South of Koreatown, COTE Korean Steakhouse is at 16 West 22nd Street in the Flatiron District, where an integrated cooktop — a grill set into each table, under its own spotlight — does the cooking, and the room's air filtration takes the smoke and the smell of searing beef off without an overhead hood.

faq.question: What makes a room a tabletop Korean barbecue room?
faq.answer: The grill is set into the diner's own table and the meat is cooked there, whether the party does the grilling or a server does. A gas grate, a charcoal grate and an integrated cooktop under a spotlight all meet that definition, and so does a removable grate a server swaps between rounds. A tofu house, a fried-chicken house, a steam-table deli and a tasting-menu kitchen that sends the meat out already cooked all fail it, however Korean the menu is. Cho Dang Gol, HanGawi, The Kunjip and Woorijip all trade in Koreatown, and none of them has a grill at the table.

faq.question: Where in Manhattan are the tabletop grills concentrated?
faq.answer: Thirteen of the eighteen stand inside six blocks. Six are on West 32nd Street between Fifth Avenue and Broadway: Jongro BBQ at 22, New Wonjo at 23, Antoya at 37, Jongro BBQ Market at 39, miss KOREA BBQ at 10, and Gaonnuri at 1250 Broadway with its entrance on the street. The other seven stand a block east and south. Four are on Fifth Avenue between 31st and 32nd Streets — Let's Meat at 307, Gopchang Story at 312, Nubiani at 315 and LOVE Korean BBQ at 319 — and three on the cross streets east of Fifth Avenue: Ahgassi Gopchang at 1 East 32nd Street, Dons Bogam at 17 East 32nd Street and Howoo at 7 East 31st Street.

faq.question: Which rooms burn charcoal rather than gas?
faq.answer: New Wonjo, at 23 West 32nd Street, burns charcoal instead of gas under the grill at the table. For the other seventeen the fuel is not stated. COTE Korean Steakhouse, at 16 West 22nd Street, works differently again: a cooktop is set into each table under its own spotlight, and the room's air filtration carries the smoke and the smell of searing beef away without an overhead hood.

faq.question: What are the opening hours?
faq.answer: No source states the opening hours of most of these restaurants, so none are given here. Four are stated. Jongro BBQ Market, at 39 West 32nd Street, runs 11:30 a.m. to midnight Sunday through Thursday and to 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday. Antoya, at 37 West 32nd Street, runs 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and to 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday. Dons Bogam, at 17 East 32nd Street, runs 11:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and to midnight on Friday and Saturday. Yoon Haeundae Galbi, at 8 West 36th Street, takes its last dinner seating at 9:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and at 10 p.m. on Friday and Saturday.

faq.question: Do any of these operators run a second room?
faq.answer: Three do. Nubiani runs the third floor at 315 Fifth Avenue and a second room at 243 East 58th Street. Jongro BBQ runs the second floor at 22 West 32nd Street and a room at 155-14 Roosevelt Avenue in Flushing, Queens; Jongro BBQ Market at 39 West 32nd Street is a separate door on the same block. Golden HOF absorbed NY Kimchi, the downstairs restaurant at 16 West 48th Street, in July 2025, and the grills are the downstairs room's. Insa in Gowanus and Atti in Downtown Brooklyn are Brooklyn addresses, and the Fort Lee, Palisades Park and Edgewater corridor is in Bergen County, New Jersey.

photos.title: West 32nd Street, Koreatown, Manhattan
photos.description: A wide view down the West 32nd Street canyon, with tenement and loft buildings rising on both sides and a clear strip of sky between them. Blade signs and stacked upper-floor placards project from the frontages on the right, several marked with floor numbers, and the building number 38 stands in large figures on the corner facade in the foreground.
photos.author: Kidfly182
